text: Michaela Hübschle (born 21 September 1950 as Michaela Kuntze in Otjiwarongo) is a Namibian politician and former Deputy Minister for Prisons and Correctional Services. After completing her schooling in Otjiwarongo, she studied at the University of Pretoria in South Africa from 1970 to 1973, earning a BA. She then worked as a translator for the German embassy in Pretoria until 1976. She subsequently moved to the Federal Republic of Germany, where she was active in the local environmental movement. In 1984, she returned to South West Africa (now Namibia) and worked on various projects in Katutura, a township in Windhoek. Since 2000, Hübschle has been the chairman of the Criminals Return Into Society (CRIS), which she founded; the organization was renamed Change in August 2009. CRIS is committed to start-up and life support for former prisoners and provides vocational support, and it organizes the Gildehaus, an informal forum for leading personalities from government and politics. Hübschle was a member of the Constituent Assembly of Namibia and served as a SWAPO deputy in the National Assembly from 1990 to 2000. In 1995, she was appointed Deputy Minister for Prisons and Correctional Services, a position she held until 2000. During her tenure, she implemented an AIDS prevention program offering free condoms to prisoners of conscience, although this initiative was rejected by the government, which viewed it as supporting homosexuality. For the 2000 parliamentary elections, Hübschle was not selected as a candidate after criticizing prisoner abuse in the context of the Caprivi conflict the previous year and calling for SWAPO leadership to apologize for prisoner abuse during the liberation struggle. In a 2007 article co-authored with SWAPO politician Shapua Kaukungua, Hübschle accused the party leadership of defective party-internal democracy and interventions in regional and local elections. In the 2009 parliamentary elections, Hübschle broke with SWAPO and ran for the Rally for Democracy and Progress (Namibia) (RDP), of which she is a member of the central committee, but she did not enter parliament. Her parents were the German-Namibian farmer Eberhard Kuntze and the author Lisa Kuntze. Hübschle was married to Dr. Otto Hübschle, former head of the Namibian veterinary authority, who died in 2008 at the age of 62. They had two children.
